title: Conversational Dueling Bandits in Generalized Linear Models

problem.claim: Conversational recommendation systems need to learn user preferences online through interaction and feedback.

gap.claim: Existing methods are limited by binary feedback and by contextual bandit approaches that mainly assume linear rewards, leaving relative feedback and generalized linear reward structures insufficiently addressed.

contributions.claim: The paper integrates dueling bandits with generalized linear models to introduce relative feedback into conversational recommendation systems.
The paper proposes a conversational dueling bandit algorithm called ConDuel.
The framework is extended to multinomial logit bandits with theoretical and experimental guarantees.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe ConDuel as a novel conversational dueling bandit algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report theoretical regret upper-bound analyses and empirical validation on synthetic and real-world data.
The authors report theoretical and experimental guarantees for the multinomial logit bandit extension.

narrative_sequence.summary: Conversational recommendation systems elicit preferences through interaction and use multi-armed bandits for online learning.
Existing approaches rely on binary feedback and largely linear reward assumptions, despite users having multiple choices and relative feedback being informative.
The paper introduces relative-feedback conversations through dueling bandits in generalized linear models and proposes ConDuel.
The authors report regret analysis and empirical validation on synthetic and real-world data.
The framework is extended to multinomial logit bandits with reported theoretical and experimental guarantees.

source_observation.claim: Relative feedback is presented as more informative than binary feedback for conversational recommendation.

interpretation.claim: Preference elicitation may benefit from modeling comparisons among multiple choices rather than only independent item-level approval or rejection.

application.claim: When users naturally compare alternatives, conversational recommenders could use pairwise or relative-feedback bandit interactions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when relative feedback improves performance over binary feedback or how users provide it in practice.

source_observation.claim: The paper targets non-linear reward structures represented through generalized linear models.

interpretation.claim: Bandit methods designed for linear rewards may be inadequate when reward behavior follows a generalized linear structure.

application.claim: Contextual recommendation systems with non-linear reward responses could consider generalized-linear bandit formulations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the generalized linear model assumptions or the conditions under which the method's guarantees hold.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the algorithmic details of ConDuel.
The exact regret-bound forms and assumptions are not stated.
The datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative experimental results are not specified.
The abstract does not explain the multinomial logit extension's formulation or scope.
